ex_vivo_detail: ZY4 was incubated in human plasma for up to 10 h; residual antibacterial activity against P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii was retained and 91% of intact peptide remained (SI Appendix, Figs. S4 and S5A). Classified as ex vivo because it is a plasma stability assay in plasma removed from a human body. The body labels this incubation 'in vitro'.
in_vitro_detail: Bacterial culture assays (MIC determination, killing kinetics, SEM membrane morphology, propidium iodide influx by flow cytometry, biofilm formation and eradication, persister cell killing, 60-passage resistance selection) against P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii standard and MDR clinical strains; cytotoxicity assays up to 80 uM; LPS-stimulated cytokine release in mouse RAW264.7 cells; 10 ns molecular dynamics simulations (in silico).

concentration_time_figure.note: The body cites SI Appendix Fig. S5 B and C as the source of the 1.8 h half-life and Fig. S5A for the 91% remaining after 10 h plasma incubation, but no caption or description of these panels appears in the body text, and no concentration-time plot appears in the main-text figures. Availability cannot be confirmed from the body, so it is recorded as false.

bioanalytical_quote: Bacteria preparation, MD simulations, antibacterial properties, toxicity assays, plasma stability, pharmacokinetic analysis... were performed by using standard approaches... A detailed description of materials and methods... can be found in the SI Appendix.
notes: This is a PNAS-format paper whose Materials and Methods section defers essentially all experimental detail to the SI Appendix, which is not present in this text file. Consequently the PK half-life of 1.8 h is reported in the Results body with no accompanying dose, sampling matrix, timepoints, group size, PK model, kinetic phase or bioanalytical method. The PEPLIFE2 header states mouse plasma and LC-MS/MS, but those are database metadata not supported by the body, so half_life_matrix and bioanalytical_method are left 'not reported'. The abstract gives the same half-life (1.8 h); the value recorded here is taken from the Results body sentence, not from the abstract. No one-letter sequence is printed anywhere in the body, even though Fig. 1A is described as containing the sequences. Live P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii inocula and E. coli LPS (15 mg/kg i.p.) were administered as infectious/inflammatory challenges rather than as test articles, and are therefore not listed as agents.
